claims.claim_ar: حرف التعريف في «الْحَمْدُ» يضفي عمومية وشمولاً على المقصود بالمدح؛ أي أن المدح هنا مُطلق وكامِل لا يختص بوجه واحد، بل لكل وجوه الحَمْد.
claims.claim_en: The definite article in «al‑hamd» grants the praise a sense of universality and comprehensiveness; the praise is absolute and complete, not restricted to a single aspect but encompassing all aspects of praise.
claims.needs_review_reason: No primary-source quotes provided (al-Jurjānī, al-Sakkākī, etc. not supplied). Claim is a conventional classical interpretation but must be verified against the specified sources.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Gives the opening word a totalizing, authoritative tone that frames the whole surat as praise-oriented.

claims.claim_ar: الاقتصار على كلمة واحدة «الْحَمْدُ» في افتتاح الفاتحة دليل على الإيجاز البلاغي (الإِيجاز)؛ كلمة موجزة تحوي معانٍ كثيرة وتلخّص مقاصد المدح في كلمة واحدة.
claims.claim_en: The use of a single word «al‑hamd» to open the chapter demonstrates rhetorical concision (iʿjāz); a concise word encapsulates many meanings and summarizes the purposes of praise in one term.
claims.needs_review_reason: No direct citations from the requested classical authors were provided; the observation is general and should be checked against their texts.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Conveys density of meaning and an elevated, concentrated register right at the outset.

claims.claim_ar: افتتاح السورة بلفظ «الْحَمْدُ» يعمل كقضيبٍ موضوعيٍّ يجمعُ المقاصد البلاغية للسورة؛ أي أنه تأسيس موضوعي (أسلوب حكيم) يوجّه القارئ أو السامع إلى إطار المدح والشكر كله من البداية.
claims.claim_en: Opening the surah with the term «al‑hamd» functions as an organizing theme (rhetorical wisdom/aslūb ḥakīm), setting the surah’s rhetorical framework toward praise and gratitude from the very beginning.
claims.needs_review_reason: Claim reflects common stylistic reading but lacks direct sourcing from the listed classical authorities in the provided input.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Establishes a guiding interpretive lens for the following clauses; signals the reader to interpret subsequent phrases within the register of praise.

claims.claim_ar: وضع «الْحَمْدُ» مبتدأً منصوباً للاسمية (الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ) يبرز وظيفة الكلمة كقيلولةٍ نحويةٍ وبلاغيةٍ تربط المدح بالممدوح مباشرةً (فاصل/واصل): فهي منفصلة في اللفظ لكنها متصلة بالمقام والمعنى.
claims.claim_en: Placing «al‑hamd» as the nominal subject (al‑hamd-u lillāh) highlights its function as a grammatical and rhetorical pivot (separation/joining—fasl/wasl): lexically distinct yet directly connected in meaning to the one praised.
claims.needs_review_reason: No primary-source excerpts were provided; the structural reading is standard but should be verified against the specified authors.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Highlights the syntactic prominence of praise and its immediate attribution to God, producing clarity and force in the statement.
